item.title: [7] Correlated quantum criticality and topological magnetoelectric response in Bi2Se3
item.description:
Last authors: Aniekan Magnus Ukpong

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: DFT and theory linking frustrated magnetic order to topological surface states in the TI Bi2Se3.

Tags: #material:Bi2Se3 #topology #DFT

Abstract: A defining feature of quantum materials is that multiple orders govern low-energy physics and are not independent. We study Bi$_2$Se$_3$ by combining DFT with a renormalized correlated honeycomb model in which frustrated magnetic order and helical topological surface states are coupled via one control parameter. The surface states map to a honeycomb Hubbard model with frustrated $J_1$--$J_2$ exchange. Exact diagonalization up to 20 sites shows the N\'{e}el structure factor and valence-bond-solid order parameter cross at $J_2/J_1 \approx 0.22$, agreeing with QMC/DMRG, and a dynamical spin structure factor broadens near the crossover, as expected for a spinon continuum. Band inversion of the renormalized tight-binding model occurs on the same critical locus, producing jumps in the Chern number and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant mirrored by the skyrmion charge $Q$. This gives a microscopic link: $Q$ selects the axion angle and thus the topological magnetoelectric coupling. We distinguish axion coupling, independent of skyrmion helicity, from the helicity-dependent magnetoelectric multipole coupling, whose toroidal component scales as $\sin\gamma$ and vanishes for N\'{e}el-type textures. We derive the $Q$-topological magnetoelectric energy and estimate $\sim 10^{-20}\,\mathrm{J}$ per skyrmion per cycle for few-tesla fields. The cycle is thermodynamically bounded: constant-$\theta$ cycles extract no net work, and efficiency is limited by axionic entropy change.

item.title: [8] Thermal Phase Transition of Three Dimensional Orthogonal Metals
item.description:
Last authors: Hanbit Oh, Eun-Gook Moon

Authors: Inho Song, Minsu Park, Hanbit Oh, Eun-Gook Moon

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Identifies characteristic ARPES spectral signatures for transitions in correlated orthogonal metals like Sr2VO3FeAs.

Tags: #method:ARPES #theory #correlated-electrons

Abstract: Orthogonal metals provide a paradigmatic example of strongly entangled metallic states whose transport and thermodynamic properties resemble those of conventional Fermi liquids, while their single-electron excitations remain fundamentally distinct. Despite considerable interest in their unusual ground-state properties, orthogonal metals in three spatial dimensions and their finite-temperature behavior remain relatively unexplored. Here, we investigate a three-dimensional orthogonal metal and characterize the thermodynamic and spectroscopic signatures associated with its finite-temperature phase transition. Starting from a simple model of fermions coupled to spin degrees of freedom, we perturbatively demonstrate that the thermal transition known to occur in the purely bosonic limit persists in the presence of coupling to a gapless Fermi surface. We then examine physical observables that change prominently between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes. In particular, we calculate the evolution of the physical-electron spectral function and identify characteristic signatures in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find a pronounced contrast in low-energy spectral weight between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes without requiring conventional symmetry-breaking order. Our results establish finite-temperature orthogonal-metal physics as a possible mechanism for pseudogap-like behavior in three-dimensional and quasi-two-dimensional layered materials with non-negligible interlayer hopping, which may be applied to the recent experiments in $\mathrm{Sr_2 VO_3 Fe As}$.

item.title: [7] Collective Modes of Fractional States Beyond Landau Levels
item.description:
Last authors: Peleg Emanuel, Yuval Oreg

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical framework for magnetoroton and collective modes in fractional Chern insulators and quantum Hall states.

Tags: #theory #topological #Chern-insulator

Abstract: Collective modes provide a powerful probe into the properties and stability of topologically ordered and strongly interacting phases of matter, such as fractional quantum Hall states. Yet, the description of fractional-state excitations away from the Landau-level limit remains a formidable challenge. We develop a framework for describing collective excitations in the strong-coupling regime of coupled-wire constructions and show that they emerge as solitons and breathers of effective sine-Gordon theories. This approach provides a systematic route to studying collective modes in a broad class of fractional states. Applied to a coupled-wire construction of the fractional quantum Hall effect, the framework captures key features of the magnetoroton branch. It naturally extends to fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating that magnetoroton-like collective modes persist well beyond the Landau-level limit. We find that the magnetoroton gap increases as the Fubini-Study metric approaches the ideal (trace-condition) limit, highlighting the important role of quantum geometry in the stability of fractionalized phases and their collective excitations. The same trend favors the stability of the long-wavelength quadrupolar mode associated with the chiral graviton. Together, these results identify a distinct interplay between fractionalization and quantum geometry, and provide an analytical framework for studies of collective excitations in fractional topological matter.

item.title: [10] Coexisting Kondo and Weyl-like transport in kagome heavy-fermion metal, YbyCo3Ge3-xSnx
item.description:
Last authors: M. E. Kamminga, S. Wiedmann, J. Y. Chan, M. N. Ali

Authors: M. P. Dubbelman, R. Meduri, T. M. Kyrk, Z. Cheng, P. Maderson, D. Pizzirani, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct experimental study using ARPES and transport on a novel kagome Weyl-Kondo system.

Tags: #method:ARPES #material:Yb_yCo3Ge_{3-x}Sn_x #kagome #Weyl

Abstract: Strong electron correlations and topology offer complementary routes to controlling electrical conduction, as correlations can make electrons heavy (e.g. Kondo lattices) whereas topology can make them behave as massless particles (e.g. Dirac or Weyl systems), and having both in one material is rare. In Kondo lattice systems, Kondo hybridization between localized 4$f$ and conduction electrons strongly enhances the quasiparticle mass, where in Weyl-Kondo systems these Kondo-renormalized bands form Weyl states, and simultaneous signs of both Kondo and Weyl states in one material have not been observed in transport. Here we report signs of both in the kagome metal \ce{Yb_yCo3Ge_{3-x}Sn_x} by combining magnetotransport, heat capacity, magnetization, angle-resolved and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, and DFT+U calculations to reveal Yb-dependent Kondo scattering developing into lattice coherence, with extrapolated Sommerfeld coefficient of approximately 2 ~Jmol$_{\mathrm{Yb}}^{-1}$K$^{-2}$. Transverse magnetoresistance (MR) follows single-ion Kondo scaling, whereas longitudinal transport contains an additional negative response proportional to B$^2$ and remains unsaturated up to 32 T, consistent with a chiral anomaly. These findings support a picture of Kondo and Weyl-like conduction arising from distinct electronic states without external Fermi-level tuning, suggesting a possible route to combining correlated and topological functionality in a bulk material.

item.title: [8] Repulsion-Driven Topological Superconductivity in Twisted MoTe2
item.description:
Last authors: Taige Wang, Daniel E. Parker

Authors: Tianle Wang, Tomohiro Soejima, Norman Y. Yao, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: DMRG evidence for chiral topological superconductivity and Majorana modes in twisted MoTe2 moire bands.

Tags: #material:MoTe2 #moire #topological-superconductivity #Majorana

Abstract: We show that a microscopic model of twisted MoTe$_2$ with screened Coulomb interactions produces topological superconductivity. Using the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) on infinite cylinders, we find that the narrow Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ has Cooper pair correlations that strengthen with cylinder circumference, consistent with two dimensional superconductivity. The superconductor has chiral $f$-wave pairing around the valley center, and its topology produces chiral Majorana edge modes and non-Abelian vortex cores. At zero displacement field, the superconductor spans fillings $-0.78\lesssim\nu\lesssim-0.72$, close to the experimental range, and extends in a dome to finite displacement field. We then predict how its stiffness evolves with the filling and the tunable displacement field. The interplay with screening length is also examined. Nearby, we find a fractional Chern insulator, a topological charge density wave, a metal, and a charge-ordered state. The last is a candidate for the reentrant integer Hall regime in experiments. These results establish a route from repulsive interactions in microscopic models of moir\'e materials to chiral topological uperconductors with chiral Majorana edge modes.

item.title: [7] Possibility of Potts Spin-Ice in Rare Earth Twisted-Kagome Layers: an Example of DyAgGe
item.description:
Last authors: Hari Bhandari, Nirmal J. Ghimire

Authors: Gunnar F. Schwertfeger, Po-Hao Chang, Predrag Nikolic, Igor I. Mazin, Hari Bhandari, Nirmal J. Ghimire

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Investigates new magnetic phases in twisted kagome layers of DyAgGe.

Tags: #material:DyAgGe #kagome #spin-ice

Abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spin-ice compounds, predominantly based on the pyrochlore or spinel structure, have been attracting considerable interest in the last two decades. A two-dimensional (2D) analogue is the spin-ice consisting of kagome planes. So far, only Ising spin ice has been discovered in any material, and only one 2D material, the kagome compound HoAgGe, has been identified as a spin ice. In this Letter, we show that another rare-earth twisted Kagome magnetic compound, DyAgGe, is in fact a Potts spin ice (or color ice), where at each site not two but four spin directions are allowed. We argue that an 8-state spin ice may also exist in this class of systems. We present a first-principles calculation of magnetic interactions in DyAgGe, and confirm the 4-state Potts structure of this material by matching our model predictions with the available experimental data.

item.title: [9] Constraining the Superconducting Gap of Monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3 via Statistical Analysis and Tip-Height-Dependent Tunneling Spectroscopy
item.description:
Last authors: Hanno H. Weitering, Wonhee Ko

Authors: Dongwon Shin, Xiyou Peng, Kaleb McClure, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-precision STS study of the superconducting gap in monolayer FeSe, a key unconventional superconductor.

Tags: #method:STS #material:FeSe/SrTiO3 #superconductivity

Abstract: Monolayer FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (001) exemplifies interface-enhanced superconductivity, exhibiting a transition temperature nearly ten times that of bulk FeSe. Yet, its tunneling spectra lack clearly identifiable superconducting coherence peaks, preventing an unambiguous determination of the gap magnitude. Here, we use ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy as a function of temperature, tip-sample separation, and lateral position to disentangle tunneling contributions by statistical analysis. Decay rates extracted by regression of tip-height-dependent spectroscopy reveal three energy regimes: Andreev-reflection-dominated tunneling below 6 meV, mixed Andreev and quasiparticle tunneling between 6 and 13 meV, and predominantly quasiparticle tunneling above 13 meV. Spatially resolved spectroscopy and correlation analysis further reveal that the tunneling conductance is predominantly localized near defects below 6 meV but becomes spatially extended at higher energies. Together, these results constrain the superconducting gap to lie between 6 and 13 meV. Our findings establish statistical analysis of spectroscopy as a powerful approach to constraining superconducting gap structures when complex spectral features prevent the unambiguous identification of coherence peaks.

item.title: [7] Korringa factor in Dirac-nodal-line systems
item.description:
Last authors: Takahiko Sekine, Kanoda Kazushi

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical analysis of NMR signatures in Dirac nodal-line topological semimetals.

Tags: #theory #Dirac-semimetal #topology

Abstract: The Korringa factor $K(\alpha)$ in the nuclear magnetic resonance studies is a widely used measure of electron-correlation effects in metals and is conventionally interpreted using the non-correlated value $K(\alpha)$ = 1. In Dirac-fermion systems, however, the non-correlated reference value depends on the electronic density of states (DOS) and differs from that of conventional metals. Here, we theoretically investigate the non-correlated Korringa factor $K^*(\alpha)$ in a Dirac nodal-line (DNL) system with finite nodal-line dispersion using a DOS-based approach. We show that $K^*(\alpha)$ exhibits an intrinsic temperature dependence, continuously evolving from the Dirac-fermion value of 1.71 at high temperatures to the metallic value of 1 at low temperatures. The crossover temperature is found to be proportional to the nodal-line dispersion width, identified as the characteristic energy scale governing the non-correlated Korringa factor in DNL systems. We further demonstrate that Landau quantization generates singular DOS structures that strongly enhance $K^*(\alpha)$, producing pronounced peaks even in the absence of electron correlations. In addition, $K^*(\alpha)$ exhibits two distinct types of magnetic oscillations arising from intra-level and inter-level contributions. The latter originates from the overlap of singular points belonging to positive and negative quantum-number Landau subbands at the Fermi level and represents a unique consequence of the finite energy dispersion of a DNL. These results provide a quantitative reference for interpreting NMR experiments in DNL materials and for identifying genuine correlation effects beyond DOS-induced contributions.

item.title: [10] Dynamical Phonon Anharmonicity Drives Charge-Density-Wave Softening and Electronic Quasiparticle Decoherence in Monolayer 1H-NbSe2
item.description:
Last authors: Yi Xia

Score 10/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relates phonon softening to electronic quasiparticle signatures and CDW in a primary material of interest, NbSe2.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #material:NbSe2 #CDW #electronic-structure #theory

Abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) instabilities in two-dimensional materials are governed by strongly anharmonic soft phonons, whose dynamical behavior remains poorly understood beyond the statically renormalized vibrations. Here, using monolayer 1H-NbSe2, we investigate how frequency-dependent three- and four-phonon interactions reshape phonon spectral functions and influence electronic excitations. We find that three-phonon interactions induce substantial dynamical softening of CDW modes, increasing the estimated transition temperature relative to static self-consistent phonon theory. Four-phonon interactions further promote such dynamical softening and enhance spectral broadening, producing non-Lorentzian lineshapes that challenge the quasiparticle picture. Incorporating dynamically renormalized phonon frequencies and electron-phonon coupling into Fan-Migdal electron self-energy calculations reveals enhanced electronic kinks, satellite features, and momentum-dependent quasiparticle decoherence, driven by the strong momentum dependence of the electron-phonon coupling matrix elements. These findings establish dynamical anharmonicity as a critical link between soft-mode lattice fluctuations and electronic spectral signatures, providing insights into coupled lattice-electron dynamics in two-dimensional quantum materials.

item.title: [8] Resolving magnetic order and dynamics with polarized neutron scattering: a practical guide to longitudinal polarization analysis
item.description:
Last authors: Sijie Xu, Pengcheng Dai

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Comprehensive review of neutron scattering techniques applied to altermagnets and kagome magnets.

Tags: #method #neutron-scattering #altermagnetism #kagome

Abstract: Neutron scattering provides microscopic information on magnetic order and spin dynamics. Most experiments, however, use unpolarized neutrons and do not fully exploit the information carried by the neutron spin. Longitudinal polarization analysis (LPA), established in the pioneering work of Moon, Riste, and Koehler at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in the late 1960s, separates magnetic and nonmagnetic scattering contributions through their different effects on the neutron spin. In this review, we illustrate how LPA can distinguish weak magnetic scattering from nonmagnetic contributions, constrain small moment components, and resolve the spin-space anisotropy of magnetic excitations. We introduce the formalism connecting measured polarization channels to magnetic quantities and discuss scattering geometry, crystallographic projections, and corrections for finite polarization. Our aim is to provide a practical guide for neutron scatterers using LPA to determine magnetic structures and characterize spin excitations in quantum materials. We conclude with opportunities in altermagnets, unconventional superconductors, and kagome magnets.

Abstract: We investigate the electronic structure, local orbital coupling, and strain-tunable nonlinear Hall response of two arsenic-substituted borophosphene-derived monolayers, As@MBP and As@AMBP, using first-principles calculations and tight-binding analysis. item.title: [7] Why strong spin-orbit coupling does not destabilize the Dirac spin liquid in the Yb delafossites
item.description:
Last authors: Yasir Iqbal

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of Dirac spin liquids in delafossites with comparison to kagome systems and neutron data.

Tags: #theory #Yb-delafossites #spin-liquid

Abstract: The Yb delafossites NaYbSe$_2$, KYbSe$_2$, CsYbSe$_2$ and NaYbO$_2$ are candidates for the U(1) Dirac spin liquid (DSL) of the triangular lattice. Strong spin-orbit coupling gives their exchange an XXZ anisotropy $\Delta$ and bond-dependent couplings $J_{\pm\pm}$, $J_{z\pm}$ that lock the spin frame to the lattice. We show that, within a single layer of a stable Heisenberg DSL, these couplings generate no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator of their own. Inversion at the bond centers removes the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya channel that gaps the kagome DSL, so the locked symmetry forbids a mass, density or current at any order and, assuming continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. Every Lorentz-scalar four-fermion operator induced by spin-orbit coupling shares an SU(4) multiplet, and hence its scaling dimension, with a Heisenberg-allowed one, and the nine non-scalar quartics without such a partner arise only at second order and are irrelevant at large $N$. The Heisenberg DSL itself allows a Lorentz-vector quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, which a stable phase must also render irrelevant. Beyond a single layer, spin-orbit coupling opens an interlayer monopole channel in rhombohedral stacking. If the Heisenberg DSL is instead multicritical, an anisotropy as small as that of KYbSe$_2$ matters only below tens of mK. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, and exact diagonalization indicates that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not yet fix the K-point exponent, and gapless out-of-plane spin fluctuations at the K point would test the chiral-Ising selection.

item.description:
Last authors: Yasir Iqbal

Symmetry forbids every Dirac mass, density and current at any order and, assuming adiabatic continuity, any new monopole term through charge three. At linear order the couplings reach only spin-2 members of the quartic multiplets $\mathbf{20}'$ and $\mathbf{84}$, which share their dimensions with Heisenberg-allowed operators. At second order $J_{\pm\pm}$ and $J_{z\pm}$ renormalize the anisotropy through $J_{z\pm}^2-2J_{\pm\pm}^2$, and nine spin-1 quartics without Heisenberg partners appear, irrelevant at $O(1/N)$. A single layer of a stable Heisenberg spin liquid thus acquires no relevant Lorentz-scalar operator from spin-orbit coupling. The Heisenberg liquid itself allows a Lorentz-vector $\mathbf{20}'$ quartic of large-$N$ dimension 2.92, with two-loop $\epsilon$-expansion estimates 2.9-3.5. Rhombohedral stacking adds triplet-monopole tunneling between layers at first order. At the transition to 120$^\circ$ order the anisotropy is relevant, with crossover exponent $y_T\simeq0.74$-1, and exact diagonalization shows that easy-plane anisotropy selects the chiral-Ising class. The out-of-plane spectrum at the K point then stays gapless, and the spin-flip to non-spin-flip ratio grows as $\omega^{-0.56}$ at leading order. Existing KYbSe$_2$ neutron data below $J$ do not fix the K-point exponent. item.description:
Last authors: Xiaojun Wu, Jinlong Yang

Authors: Peibo Xu, Yixuan Che, Yuxuan Li, Haifeng Lv, Xiaojun Wu, Jinlong Yang

Why: Theoretical exploration of hybrid spin splitting in altermagnets and compensated magnets.

Abstract: Nonrelativistic spin splitting in collinear compensated magnets is constrained by spin-group symmetry, with distinct alternating and Zeeman-type splitting typically associated with altermagnets and fully compensated ferrimagnets, respectively. From a spin-density perspective, we propose a class of hybrid compensated magnets in which alternating-like and Zeeman-type spin splitting coexist within a single collinear compensated state. Using a minimal two-sector model, we demonstrate that this coexistence arises from competition between directional sublattice dispersion and the sector-dependent energy biases arising from the same structural inequivalence. These results connect the spatial organization of spin density with the electronic response to structural inequivalence, providing a design principle for hybrid spin splitting in compensated magnets.

Abstract: We investigate the effects of ionic hydrogen (H$^+$) intake on the occupied and unoccupied states of MnSb$_2$Te$_4$, a van der Waals magnetic material. item.description:
Last authors: Jinsheng Wen, Wei Li

Why: Study of multipolar order in a triangular lattice magnet using neutron scattering analysis.

Abstract: The absence of magnetic Bragg peaks and a broad excitation continuum are commonly recognized experimental features of a quantum spin liquid. The Ce-based triangular-lattice hexaaluminate CeMgAl$_{11}$O$_{19}$ exhibits both signatures, yet its effective model and ground state remain under debate. We further propose nuclear spin-lattice relaxation and spin-current experiments to probe the gapless excitations of this hidden triakontadipole superfluid. Our findings thus open a new avenue for high-rank multipolar physics in rare-earth triangular-lattice magnets.

item.description:
Last authors: Bijay Kumar Sahoo, Abhiram Soori

Why: Theoretical study of transport in altermagnet-TI heterostructures, both core interest topics.

Conversely, when asymmetric chemical potentials are applied ($\mu_t \neq \mu_b$), this symmetry is broken, yielding a finite transverse response even for an in-plane N\'eel vector. Furthermore, we demonstrate that while the longitudinal differential conductivity exhibits Fabry-P\'erot-type oscillations as a function of the TI's chemical potential, the transverse conductivity displays a distinct antisymmetric dependence. Spatially, the transverse current contribution decays exponentially with position inside the TI region. We also find that both the longitudinal and transverse differential conductivity exhibit periodic oscillations with the junction parameter $\chi_t=\chi_b$. Last authors: Erkki L\"ahderanta, Sebastiaan van Dijken

Why: Transport study involving YIG and VO2, a correlated oxide with insulator-to-metal transition.

Tags: #experiment #VO2 #magnonics

Abstract: Electrically reconfigurable spin-wave transport is central to realizing energy-efficient magnonic information technologies, yet existing current-driven approaches require current densities that undermine the fundamental dissipation advantage of spin-wave-based signal processing. Why: Study of a layered magnetic metallic compound with interesting Fermi surface and correlation effects.

Abstract: The structural, electronic, and physical properties of previously unexplored layered tetragonal compound SrMn$_2$Ge$_2$ are reported. The compound crystallizes in the ThCr$_2$Si$_2$-type structure with a crystallographic parameters $c/a$ ratio of $2.535(3)$, significantly smaller than those of the related BaMn$_2$$Pn_2$ compounds ($Pn =$ P, As, Sb, Bi), indicating enhanced interlayer interaction between the moment-bearing Mn-ions. item.title: [8] Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
item.description:
Last authors: Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Highly relevant theory on Berry curvature and quantum metric isolation in Dirac semimetals.

Tags: #theory #material #topologicalsemimetal

Abstract: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.

Abstract: Periodic deformations flatten electronic bands of graphene which could host strongly correlated electrons similar to those observed in twisted graphene bilayers. Abstract: A comprehensive spectroscopic map of the electronic, magnetic, and lattice excitations is presented for the bilayer nickelate La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ using Raman scattering at ambient pressure. item.title: [9] Loss of altermagnetic order and smooth restoration of Kramers' spin degeneracy with increasing temperature in CrSb and MnTe
item.description:
Last authors: Arthur Ernst, Julie B. Staunton

Authors: Christopher D. Woodgate, Nabil Menai, Arthur Ernst, Julie B. Staunton

Why: Theoretical and spectroscopic implications of altermagnetic order in CrSb and MnTe.

Tags: #theory #material #altermagnetism

Abstract: We describe how thermally induced spin fluctuations modify the electronic structures of two prototypical altermagnets, CrSb and MnTe, via application of the disordered local moment picture. For both materials, our self-consistent, ab initio calculations demonstrate that local magnetic moments persist on Cr and Mn atoms in their paramagnetic states, necessitating a spin-polarised description of the electronic structure even above the N\'eel temperature, $T_\mathrm{N}$. Moreover, Kramers' spin degeneracy, which is broken for both materials in their altermagnetic ground states, is shown to be smoothly restored - on the average - as the local moments thermally disorder. By contrast, in semiconducting MnTe, with its band gap largely unaffected by magnetic disorder, the spin degeneracy only returns at temperatures close to and above $T_\mathrm{N}$. We quantify the temperature dependence of the altermagnetic order parameter and the underlying electronic structures of both materials, with implications for their spin transport and spectroscopic properties.

Abstract: We identify two fundamental properties of the Gor'kov Green's function of finite one-dimensional topological superconductors. We further predict a characteristic in-plane conductivity anisotropy that serves as a definitive transport fingerprint to discriminate KHW states with distinct ordering wavevectors. Our work provides a microscopic foundation for the newly observed KHW order and establishes a unified theoretical framework for understanding emergent modulated hybridization phenomena in heavy fermion materials.

item.title: [7] Chiral Superconductivity Adjacent to a Wigner Crystal in Rhombohedral Graphene
item.description:
Last authors: Ke Wang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Addresses electronic correlations and chiral pairing in rhombohedral graphene, a topic of interest.

Tags: #material #theory #graphene #superconductivity

Abstract: It was experimentally observed that Wigner-crystal and chiral superconducting phases occur adjacent to each other in rhombohedral graphene. In this Letter, we explore electronic correlations underlying the two phases and identify the pairing mechanism of chiral superconductivity. Exchange correlations play an essential role in both phases. First, we use self-consistent Hartree-Fock calculations to identify a Wigner-crystal state. Second, to investigate the pairing mechanism, we go beyond charge screening and construct a particle-hole-renormalized interaction through the coupled parquet and Bethe-Salpeter equations. This interaction incorporates exchange correlations while preserving crossing symmetry. Within this framework, we find that electronic correlations in the quarter metal are strongly enhanced near the crystal phase boundary, generating an effective attraction that favors superconducting pairing. Consequently, chiral superconductivity (CSC) emerges in a narrow sliver adjacent to the crystal. Furthermore, we identify the winding number of the superconducting order parameter as $-3$, indicating its $f$-wave nature. These results connect the emergence of chiral pairing and its location in the phase diagram to the electronic correlations favoring crystallization.

item.description:

Why: High-quality growth of a kagome Weyl semimetal with giant anomalous Hall; directly targets core interests.

Tags: #method #material #kagome #Weylsemimetal

Abstract: Materials with chemical identity Mn3X, where X is Sn, Ga, or Ge, are Heusler alloys with intriguing properties that are fundamentally and technologically interesting. They have topological properties with a non-trivial band structure that identify them as Weyl semimetals in the bulk. Their magnetic properties, which give rise to the topological band structure through spin-orbit coupling, are determined by their Kagome lattice structure, making them chiral non-collinear antiferromagnets. Among these materials, Mn3Ge is particularly interesting because it has a larger Berry curvature, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity and motivating potential spintronic applications. The desirable properties are only obtained when Mn3Ge has the D019 crystal structure, so producing an easily reproducible growth recipe is the main objective of this paper. Here we show that ultra-high-quality thin films of Mn3Ge with D019 symmetry can be grown from a Mn5Ge target on an Al2O3(0001) substrate with a Ru(0001) seed layer. The expected non-collinear antiferromagnetic order was confirmed by the finding of weak zero-field magnetisation $\mathrm{(0.0086 \pm 0.0002) \mu_{B}/Mn}$ that does not saturate at high magnetic fields and has a Neel temperature of $\mathrm{(291 \pm 2)\, K}$.

item.title: [7] Chiral phonon magnetism from localized Raman excitation
item.description:
Last authors: Yuhan Wang, Chuanshan Tian

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of chiral phonon-induced magnetism using THz and MOKE spectroscopy.

Tags: #experiment #phonon #magnetism #spectroscopy

Abstract: Optically driven chiral phonons can induce transient magnetism in non-magnetic crystals, yet the microscopic relationship between phonon angular momentum and the resulting magnetic response remains unresolved. Here we distinguish the roles of pseudo-angular momentum and mechanical angular momentum in tetragonal {\alpha}-TeO2. Combining phase-resolved terahertz spectroscopy with magneto-optical Kerr measurements (MOKE), we reconstruct the motion of a doubly degenerate phonon and continuously control its angular momentum. The MOKE response follows the sign and magnitude of phonon angular momentum as well as its dynamics, whereas non-rotating phonons, including those with finite pseudo-angular momentum, produce no detectable magnetic signal. The MOKE rotation corresponds to an effective magnetic field of approximately 14 mT, nearly seven orders of magnitude above the estimate for spatially uniform ionic currents. Moreover, the Kerr response scales linearly with the emitted terahertz field, rather than quadratically as predicted by the uniform-current model. A localized Raman-excitation model involving Te lone-pair states accounts for this scaling and yields a comparable field magnitude with the MOKE data when electronic enhancement is included. These findings identify mechanical lattice rotation as the dominant dynamical variable for the observed magnetic response and suggest that localized Raman coupling contributes to its unexpectedly large magnitude.

item.title: [8] Theory of Berry Singularity Markers: Diagnosing Topological Phase Transitions via Lock-In Tomography
item.description:
Last authors: Panagiotis Kotetes

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: New theoretical diagnostic for topological transitions with experimental (lock-in) relevance.

Tags: #topological #theory #Berry-curvature

Abstract: This work brings forward an alternative approach for inferring the topological character of phase transitions in insulators. The method relies on subjecting the system of interest to a set of external fields which consist of two parts, i.e., a weak spatiotemporally slowly-varying component on top of a constant offset. This process maps the Berry singularities dictating the bulk band structure of the insulator to a synthetic space spanned by the control parameters of the external fields. By measuring the response of the system to the weak part of the perturbations, when these are additionally chosen to form spacetime textures, one can construct a quantity that is here-termed Berry singularity marker (BSM). The BSM enables the Berry singularity detection as it becomes nonzero only in the close vicinity of a Berry singularity and is equal to its charge. Moreover, near the Berry singularities, the BSM encodes the quantum metric tensor of the system. An advantage of the present method is that it can be implemented in a lock-in fashion, thus allowing to ``filter out'' disorder effects, therefore opening the door to the resilient diagnosis of topological phase transitions.

item.description:
Last authors: Jan J. Arlt, Georg M. Bruun

Authors: Pietro Massignan, Richard Schmidt, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, et al.

Published as: Rev. Mod. Phys. DOI

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Review of polaron physics in 2D materials, relevant to correlated systems.

Tags: #review #2D-materials #polarons

Abstract: In this work we provide a comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental studies of the properties of polarons formed by mobile impurities strongly interacting with quantum many-body systems. We present a unified perspective on the universal concepts and theoretical techniques used to characterize polarons in two distinct platforms, ultracold atomic gases and atomically-thin transition metal dichalcogenides, which are linked by many deep parallels. We review polarons in both fermionic and bosonic environments, highlighting their similarities and differences including the intricate interplay between few- and many-body physics. Various kinds of polarons with long-range interactions or in magnetic backgrounds are discussed, and the theoretical and experimental progress towards understanding interactions between polarons is described. We outline how polaron physics, regarded as the low density limit of quantum mixtures, provides fundamental insights regarding the phase diagram of complex condensed matter systems. Furthermore, we describe how polarons may serve as quantum sensors of many-body physics in complex environments. Our work highlights the open problems, identifies new research directions and provides a comprehensive framework for this rapidly evolving research field.

Abstract: We study an infinite-range coupled electronic-pseudospin and nuclear-spin model for ferroquadrupolar and nuclear-spin ordering in TmVO$_4$ in external magnetic and strain fields. This material is an experimental realization of a transverse-field Ising model, where the Ising degree of freedom is quadrupolar and non-magnetic, but a transverse component is magnetic and couples both to external magnetic fields and to the nuclear spins via a hyperfine coupling. At zero external magnetic field, the electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom undergo well-separated two-stage ordering, accompanied by the release of their respective entropies. A transverse magnetic field polarizes the electronic orbital moments and, via the hyperfine coupling, the nuclear spins. The quadrupolar ordering temperature is gradually reduced to zero. However, the nuclear transition is replaced by a crossover at nonzero magnetic field. Quantum fluctuations are enhanced near the phase transitions and lead to peaks in the magnetic susceptibility. The spectral functions reveal a softening of a low-energy mode near the quantum critical point, consistent with the closing of the excitation gap and its reopening in the disordered phase. These features provide direct dynamical signatures of the field-driven quantum critical phenomena.

Abstract: We design a lattice model of a "mixed" U(1) gauge field coupled to fermions with a flavor chemical potential and solve it with large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations. In this mixed construction, dynamical magnetic monopole events are suppressed in the temporal-continuum limit. For zero flavor chemical potential, the model realizes three-dimensional quantum electrodynamics (QED$_3$) which has been argued to describe the ground state and low-energy excitations of the Dirac spin liquid phase of quantum antiferromagnets. At finite flavor chemical potential, which corresponds to a Zeeman field perturbing the Dirac spin liquid, we find a "chiral flux" phase which is characterized by the generation of a finite mean emergent gauge flux and, accordingly, the formation of relativistic Landau levels for the Dirac fermions. Because of spin-flux attachment this mode would contribute to the low-energy longitudinal spin response. Why: Superconducting correlations in moiré domain-wall networks relate to strongly correlated electron systems.

Tags: #superconduct #twisted #topological

Abstract: Extended domain-wall networks that emerge in moir\'e materials provide a distinct platform for quasi-one-dimensional electronic states. However, the interaction-driven orders in confined networks remain largely unexplored. We first analyze the system within the framework of an infinite-size theory and show that inter-ring SC-pair tunneling is renormalization-group relevant in an appropriate interaction regime, favoring enhanced SC correlations through inter-ring phase locking. item.title: [7] Quantum phase fluctuations quench chiral superconductivity in twisted overdoped cuprate bilayers
item.description:
Last authors: Miao Liu, Sheng Meng

Authors: Yin Shi, Mengxian Zhao, Fei Yang, Miao Liu, Sheng Meng

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important discussion on chiral superconductivity and transport in twisted cuprate bilayers.

Tags: #cuprate #superconduct #transport

Abstract: Twisted cuprate bilayers have been proposed to host chiral superconductivity at temperatures comparable to their large pairing scale, yet experimental signatures of broken time-reversal symmetry remain unclear. We show that quantum phase fluctuations strongly suppress chiral order in twisted overdoped cuprate bilayers despite robust intralayer pairing. At a $45^\circ$ twist, we analytically demonstrate that the chiral transition temperature obeys $T_\chi\propto t^4$ when the single-electron interlayer tunneling amplitude $t$ is weak. This collapse originates from competition between the small Josephson energy scale supporting chirality and the temperature-dependent collective zero-point energy. Chirality consequently survives only in a narrow angular window at ultralow temperatures, with relative-phase plasma softening above the chiral transition. A distinct transport signature arising from the quantum phase fluctuations is a pronounced low-temperature enhancement of the critical current near a magic angle. These findings separate pairing and chiral ordering scales and offer a possible explanation for the difficulty of observing robust chiral superconductivity in twisted cuprates.

Abstract: Chiral superconductors should carry Majorana modes along their edges, yet three decades of work on candidate materials have not measured the integer that counts them. Rhombohedral graphene offers a new route, because its superconductivity coexists with magnetic domains that can be imaged and rewritten. Here we show how heat transport can read this integer and test it against the domain pattern. Warping and finite pair momentum can close the excitation gap while the band Chern number stays fixed. An exact two-band thermal kernel shows how quantization is then lost and bounds the plateau error when the gap survives. Real-space calculations with disorder show that the integer survives disorder several times larger than the gap, because a mobility gap remains. Bogoliubov pockets instead turn the bulk into a heat conductor, and disorder does not restore quantization. Time-reversed domains should show opposite plateaux, and with ideal contacts a wall between them should carry twice either plateau. In microscopic calculations, a written wall carries this number of Majorana channels even when its core is metallic. Writing, moving and erasing such walls would test superconducting topology, its link to magnetism, and protected heat flow in one device.

This conversion parallels the recovery of three-dimensional altermagnetism through suitable periodic stacking of two-dimensional type-IV magnets. item.title: [7] Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling
item.description:
Last authors: Seth Ariel Tongay, Itai Epstein

Authors: Saroj Poudyal, Anabel Atash Kahlon, Michael Klein, et al.

Why: Important spectroscopy/optics development for 2D heterostructure excitons.

Abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers possess unique dipolar properties, providing a path for exploring correlated many-body phases, electrically tunable dipole-dipole interactions, and long-range exciton transport. However, the large electron-hole separation underlying their dipolar character also results in a significantly reduced oscillator strength, limiting their direct optical interaction with light, and thus the direct probing of their dynamics and many-body interactions. Here, we show that by using Purcell engineering of critical coupling, a weak interlayer transition can absorb as strongly as the dominant intralayer transition, despite its much smaller intrinsic oscillator strength. Using this approach, in an open cavity architecture we demonstrate an order of magnitude IX absorption modulation in bilayer and trilayer MoS2, with doubling of the IX to A-exciton interaction strength weight from ~23% to ~53%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in a tailored closed cavity architecture, the IX enhancement can reach beyond an order of magnitude, from ~5% to ~83% excitonic absorption, enabling IX absorption similar to intralayer excitons. An analytical description of the interaction is obtained via a closed-form transmission-line model which separates the excitonic and photonic contributions to the optical response, revealing how cavity architecture can be designed towards critical coupling. Our findings establish Purcell engineering of critical coupling as a general route to controlling and enhancing weak excitonic transitions.

item.title: [8] Momentum-selective graphene spectroscopy of moir\'e excitons
item.description:
Last authors: Katsunori Wakabayashi

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant spectroscopy of moiré excitons in heterostructures using graphene as a probe.

Tags: #graphene #moiré #spectroscopy

Abstract: Far-field photoluminescence probes only the light-cone corner of an exciton's momentum content, whereas energy transfer to nearby graphene integrates in-plane momenta up to the inverse spacer thickness $1/z$. For a WSe$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterobilayer we build the transition polarization $\bm{P}_n(\qv)$ of each localized moir\'e exciton from the registry-dependent vector dipole texture and use each $\bm{P}_n$ for both baths. The two baths rank the states differently: the graphene-rate ratios differ from the optical ones, their ordering inverts with spacer thickness, and the distance exponents at $z=10$\,nm spread by more than two units. These ratios are independent of the transition-dipole prefactor. Within the $C_3$-symmetric leading-harmonic model the chiral $p_+$ and $d_-$ states are also dark at normal incidence yet transfer to graphene at rates comparable to the bright ground state. Their graphene rate depends on the sign of the texture phase, a quantity invisible in far-field emission, which we determine from first principles. In a device this prediction requires a splitting, larger than the symmetry-breaking mixing, that protects the chiral partners. Graphene proximity thus acts as a momentum-selective near-field probe of moir\'e excitons, and we propose its use as a practical spectroscopy.

item.description:
Last authors: Massimo Capone, Adriano Amaricci

Why: Study of Mott/pseudogap physics using CDMFT, highly relevant to strongly correlated electron systems.

Tags: #Mott #Hubbard #CDMFT

Abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.

item.description:
Last authors: Roy W. Chantrell, Richard F. L. Evans

Authors: Jackson L. Ross, Sarah Jenkins, Ricardo Rama-Eiroa, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magnetism study on Mn2Au, relevant to antiferromagnetic spintronics interest.

Tags: #antiferromagnet #spintronics #magnetism

Abstract: Mn$_2$Au is one of the most promising materials for antiferromagnetic spintronics due to its high N\'eel temperature, moderate anisotropy, layered spin structure allowing current induced spin-orbit-torques, and ultrafast spin dynamics. Further understanding and control of the magnetic order in Mn$_2$Au for ultrafast spintronics applications via ultrashort electric/optical means requires accurate understanding of how its magnetic properties depend on temperature. Here we present atomistic spin dynamics simulations of the temperature-dependent macroscopic magnetic properties of Mn$_2$Au single crystals. We introduce a spin Hamiltonian based on previous ab initio calculations which produces temperature-dependent scaling of the anisotropy constants with magnetisation consistent with Zener-Akulov-Callen-Callen power laws. The calculated temperature dependence of exchange stiffness follows a scaling law with magnetisation of $m^{1.83}_e$ , and predicts a temperature-dependent domain wall width that agrees very well with direct simulation. Our model provides an understanding of temperature-dependent magnetic properties of Mn$_2$Au that enables large-scale simulation of the working conditions of spintronic devices.

item.title: [8] Large superconducting diode effect indicates nonuniform triplet pairing in UTe2
item.description:
Last authors: Alex Levchenko, Alexander G. Eaton

Authors: Zheyu Wu, Daniel Shaffer, Dmitry V. Chichinadze, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important transport result in UTe2, relevant to unconventional superconductivity studies.

Tags: #superconductor #transport #UTe2

Abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE) is characterized by unequal critical current magnitudes for opposite-polarity current flow, owing to broken spatial-inversion and time-reversal symmetries. For a superconducting pair wavefunction to spontaneously break inversion symmetry implies the formation of Cooper pairs with nonzero momentum, yielding a nonuniform superconducting state. For singlet superconductors, the formation of such a (FFLO) state has long been understood to provide an escape from high field Pauli pair-breaking -- how and why such an effect might occur for equal spin pairing is an open question. Here we report the observation of a large SDE in bulk specimens of the three-dimensional heavy-fermion triplet superconductor UTe$_2$, with a peak diode efficiency of 33% at the high magnetic field strength of 33.6 T, representing the highest-field observation of the SDE to date. Crucially, this nonreciprocal transport is strictly confined to a narrow field regime where superconductivity coexists with a field-induced spin-polarized state near a first-order metamagnetic phase boundary. The absence of the SDE away from this slender phase-intersection argues strongly against purely extrinsic vortex pinning asymmetries. Instead, our findings indicate spontaneous inversion symmetry breaking accompanied by finite-momentum Cooper pairing. We model this behavior using a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory, demonstrating that the intertwining of magnetic and triplet superconducting orders can stabilize an odd-parity FFLO state.

Abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the first magic angle ($\theta\approx1.05^{\circ}$) hosts topological flat bands that provide a fertile ground for exploring strongly correlated phases. At smaller twist angles ($\theta<1^{\circ}$), lattice relaxation profoundly alters the moir\'e landscape. The extent to which moir\'e lattice reconstruction at different length scales affects the electronic structure through electro-mechanical coupling remains unresolved. Using scanning tunneling microscopy on small-angle TBG devices with different twist angles $\theta\approx0.3-0.7^{\circ}$, we observe a pronounced $dI/dV$ peak at the AA site of the moir\'e lattice on top of a spectrum that is asymmetric about the charge neutrality point; we visualize lattice reconstruction at moir\'e lattice length scales (20-45\,nm); and we detect a dilation of the atomic lattice at the AA sites at Angstrom length scale. We demonstrate that the inclusion of moir\'e lattice reconstruction supports compact localized heavy fermion $f-$states at AA sites whereas the inclusion of atomic lattice dilation generates a strong flexo-electric response that breaks particle-hole symmetry, pushing the $f$-states down in energy. Consequently, these heavy fermion states energetically coexist with itinerant $c$-electrons at the AB/BA sites. Our spatially resolved spectroscopic measurements visualize this coexistence, confirming the persistence of the heavy fermion model in the small-angle regime $\theta<1^{\circ}$. Our findings show that flexo-electric responses can realize qualitatively distinct electronic landscapes in moir\'e materials beyond the single-particle picture. Looking ahead, small-angle TBG could prove an ideal platform to explore the interacting large-$N$ Kondo lattice problem with high tunability of the $f-$occupation and $c-$density through twist-angle and electrostatic back gates, respectively.
